Mock responses for UI demonstration. Values are fixtures; timings are not API benchmarks.
LESSON 10 / RAG: relevance, reranking, and groundedness
RAG has separate decisions: retrieve a shortlist, judge each candidate's relevance, sort those comparable
judgments in code, and verify each generated claim against the selected evidence. A passage can discuss the
right topic without supporting the answer. Reranking cannot recover evidence absent from the shortlist.
A refund passage saying approved refunds arrive within five business days is relevant to refund timing. It
supports a claim that arrival can take up to five business days; it does not establish instant payment. Finding
an exact quote and checking its citation location are code tasks; deciding whether it supports a paraphrased
Write grounded as a Noul over one claim and its evidence. Mark unsupported details and missing evidence as false
without using outside knowledge. Grade the four claim-passage cases. Connect this verifier to the relevance
rubric you wrote in lesson 3: compare the two questions and describe where code retrieves, filters or sorts,
checks citation existence, and splits an answer into individual claims.
Name your lesson template. Edit draft creates it if it is new; testing uses the version you saved in the editor.
Characters/4 approximation; server overhead and retries can increase cost.
Keep one factual claim per check; split a multi-claim answer before calling Jev.
Use one consistent relevance criterion for each candidate in a shortlist; order the returned judgments in code.
A relevant passage is not sufficient evidence for every claim about its topic. Inspect what the passage actually
